¹ Includes the root task. ² Excludes synthetic task-entry visit events; includes followed edges whose destination is then skipped by deduplication. The complete log distinguishes both.

The clearest optimization target is invalidation scope. The domain adapter currently makes ordinary tasks observe a shared modelFacts_ token. Thus even a targeted value publication wakes unrelated goals within these examples. Resetting a dirty task clears its visited states and goal-local findings.

All three results are fully normalized, with no unresolved subscription and no failure. All inputs were parsed before the search began. There are no parser-arrival restarts in this report.

Reading the diagrams and event numbers

N1, N2, … identify actual POVs; I1, I2, … identify their infonViews. IDs are local to each example. The initial diagram shows stored forward links (reverse list links are omitted). The traversal diagram projects actual followed edges onto those POVs; an edge may change the demand at the same POV. It is a report view, not a second graph maintained by the engine.

Event numbers are sequential observations, not timestamps. P0 means the root pass has not started yet. Click an event number to inspect its exact query and model snapshot. A new task is initialized once; a later pass or task reuse does not allocate another subgoal. Set application and graph publication are separate events.

Scalar RHS

Case 2

List members and concatenation

{"A" $="B" ("C") }→{'A' 'B' 'C'}
4 root passes8 distinct tasks116 native handle steps336 diagnostic eventsfullyNormed = true

The model needs two value-producing Sets: fill $ from "B", then evaluate ("C"). A third changing Set consolidates the RHS relationship. Each publication restarts the root walk. The unchanged "A" member is entered four times.

("C") is parsed as a concatenation expression. The outer list already has size 3 before normalization; its repeated counted-size Sets do not supply new information.

Case 3

Intersection result selection

[? *10+7]→*10+7
3 root passes2 distinct tasks33 native handle steps106 diagnostic eventsfullyNormed = true

The unknown first member is only inspected for position and extent. No normalize subgoal is created for it, and it remains unknown in the final model. This is the intended demand-driven behavior.

Selection first creates an identity to the last member; a later Set obtains size, value and overlay through that identity. These two publications cause three root passes and repeated selection walks. The inner expression remains available in selectionExpression.

What to optimize next

These are conclusions about repeated work, not a measured Rubix-cube speedup. The examples are small and the observer deliberately records a full snapshot at every event.

Observed behaviorCandidate improvementCorrectness obligation
Every model publication invalidates every task created so far in these examples. The literal "A" is revisited four times.Give tasks dependencies on the facts and relations they actually read: value, size, member extent and identity adjacency. Preserve clean tasks and their pending work.A newly added useful edge must wake relevant searches. Subscribing only to currently existing edges would miss additions.
A dirty task clears visited states, child demands and goal-local findings. Existing task IDs and model writes survive, but search work is repeated.Retain still-valid findings and resume affected continuations within a task; revisit only evidence whose assumptions changed.Queued Sets based on invalidated proofs must not execute. Keep the current generation/proof safety check until a narrower replacement is established.
The list’s RHS consolidation alone causes root pass 4 and opens additional identity-return routes.Treat a representation-only consolidation as a narrower relationship change, preserving unrelated list/value findings. Consider transferring the consumed-RHS proof to the retained identity.The equality must remain searchable and must still detect future contradictory information; do not simply suppress its notification.
Intersection selection creates an identity, then value acquisition publishes separately and restarts the selection walk.Reuse a proved selection while its member extent and selection constraints remain unchanged. Publication batching could be explored after dependencies are explicit.Selecting the correct member and satisfying its constraints are distinct proofs. Batching cannot assume a newly exposed RHS will always be usable.

Recommended first experiment: narrow the shared model dependency enough that copying "B" does not restart the unchanged "A" goal or discard the pending concat visit. Compare the same traces and results before touching broader scheduling policy.

Cost ordering is visible here: the first intersection identity Set costs 9 (five traversal steps plus one creation priced at 4); copying through that identity later costs 1. The later identity Set costs 5 because the identity already exists. The problem these examples expose is repeated valid work after publications, rather than a large set of expensive alternative paths.

Method, source and reproduction

The temporary probe includes the existing generated LocalBuild/TestProteus.cpp, renames its normal test entry point, and calls GraphNormalizer::normalize followed by waitForCompletion(). No renderer, world loading, streaming input or external producer is involved.

Each input was run twice in fresh normalizer contexts: once with the diagnostic observer disabled and once enabled. Printed outputs and native handle-step signatures matched for all three: action, demand kind, argument, accumulated cost and revision. This checks the observer against the unobserved run for these inputs; it is not a whole-engine regression test or a proof that instrumentation never affects timing.

The observer adds event callbacks to a temporary copy of GraphSearch.h and reads live model snapshots. The application’s source files and binaries were not modified. State snapshots record the objects encountered so far, including an operand that becomes detached when a concatenation is replaced. Such a retained diagnostic record is not evidence of a current graph edge.

Set applied is captured before the ensuing graph publication, so the value changes at revision r and the notification appears at r+1. Goal settled can set derived isNormed metadata without a semantic publication. An unchanged representation check can still update task-local proof metadata.

Costs in the log are accumulated route costs, not elapsed time or a total charge for the whole search. Queue estimates, function-internal loops and unchosen candidate edges are not fully profiled. These diagrams show the stored links and edges actually followed, not every potential edge the adapter could expose.

Reproduce locally

The reproduction script makes a new temporary staging directory, copies the current graph headers and generated test source, instruments only the copy, builds, and runs the three cases. It requires the existing CodeDog-generated LocalBuild/TestProteus.cpp, SCons, a C++17 compiler, GMP and ICU. Exact counts apply to the captured commit; later engine changes may intentionally alter them.

bash run-probe.sh /home/bruce/devl/Proteus4
